RULEMAKING TO IMPLEMENT                       )
LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION                    )              PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSON
STANDARDS                                     )              OF TEXAS
                                              )


                             COMMENTS OF DC ENERGY TEXAS, LLC

       DC Energy Texas, LLC (“DC Energy”) appreciates the opportunity to comment in the

instant proceeding regarding the PUC’s proposed Large Load Interconnection Procedures. Each

Large Load interconnection in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (“ERCOT”) has the

potential to significantly affect market prices and operations in ERCOT. Therefore, it is vital to

provide adequate transparency regarding future Large Load interconnections to all ERCOT

market participants. DC Energy supports the proposed definition of “competitively sensitive

information” in proposed §25.194(c)(2) and respectfully requests that the Commission

emphasize to ERCOT the need for market-wide transparency in keeping with this definition in

its forthcoming order in the instant proceeding.

     Currently, ERCOT market participants are struggling to understand where and when new

Large Loads may come online. The current uncertainty impedes the market’s collective ability

to efficiently set forward prices. For example, ERCOT holds long-term Congestion Revenue

Rights auctions, which provide forward price discovery for expected congestion up to three

years into the future. This price discovery helps project developers and investors make

decisions, including where to locate generation resources, as well as hedge their potential

congestion exposure. Uncertainty raises risk premiums, which ultimately raise costs for

consumers.
      DC Energy is concerned that ERCOT may continue not to provide adequate information

regarding Large Load interconnection requests after it implements various planned revisions to

its Protocols and Planning Guide, due to misplaced concerns regarding the scope of

competitively sensitive information. DC Energy supports the definition of “competitively

sensitive information” in proposed §25.194(c)(2), particularly, the specification that certain

pieces of information are not competitively sensitive. For instance, the “identity of a large load

customer,” and “whether an interconnection request is associated with the same applicant or

affiliated entities” are not competitively sensitive information. Providing this information to

ERCOT market participants will not create a competitive disadvantage for applicants, but it will

provide market participants with a better basis to independently assess whether certain

interconnection requests may prove redundant and, as a result, the accuracy of future load

forecasts.

     DC Energy further agrees that while “exact site locations, such as parcel identifiers or

property boundaries” should be considered competitively sensitive information, “general site

location, such as load zone” or the electrically defined point of planned interconnection should

not. As recognized in the proposed definition, the general location, expected size, and the

expected timing of energization are not competitively sensitive information. Providing this

information to the market participants will not create a competitive disadvantage for

applicants; however, it is essential for market participants in ERCOT entering long-term

transactions, developing other projects, and otherwise preparing for future grid conditions.

     DC Energy respectfully requests that the Commission provide clear guidance to ERCOT in

its forthcoming order in the instant proceeding that the identity of large load interconnection



                                                2
 applicants, including information indicating whether requests are on behalf of the same entity

or affiliates, as well as the general location, expected size and expected timing of energization

are not competitively sensitive information, and are instead essential information that should

be transparent for the wider market. In particular, market participants should have

transparency regarding the expected timeline for incremental increases in load energization in

each application and as expectations change over the course of the study and interconnection

process.


                                             Respectfully submitted,
